verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents usage-based billing ('you only pay for the compute... you actually use'). Sprites sleep 'at zero compute cost' until woken, and MCP-server Machines can stop when idle, so idle time is not billed as active compute. Coverage is partial because the evidence covers Sprites and the MCP blueprint, not general Machine billing, and one claim is softened to 'cost practically nothing when idle' rather than zero. missing for 10: documented billing granularity for active vs. stopped Machines, explicit confirmation that stopped Fly Machines incur no compute charges, independent or hands-on corroboration of idle-time billing.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can pay only for active compute time rather than idle wall-clock time

citations.quote: Fly.io uses pay-as-you-go pricing - you only pay for the compute, storage, and bandwidth you actually use.
It sleeps (at zero compute cost) until you wake it on request.
Host a remote MCP server on a Fly Machine that any MCP client can reach over HTTP and that stops when idle
